newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to privatise utilities -- minister.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to privatise utilities -- minister.

text.p: The Croatian government is preparing the privatisation of some of the countries largest companies, including utilities, Privatisation Minister Ivan Penic said on Friday.
"We have recently passed a decision to prepare another large company, Koncar, for the foreign markets," Penic told an international investment conference.

Penic said the privatisation of Koncar, Croatia's largest electrical manufacturer, would be arranged via a foreign placement. Leading pharmaceutical company Pliva was privatised by foreign placement earlier this year and is listed on the London Stock Exchange.
Penic also said plans to privatise seven largest state-owned enterprises, including the national oil and power utilities as well as telecoms, railways and others, were in the works.
"According to some proposals 30 percent of their equity would be used to support pension reform, but this still has to be regulated by law," Penic said.
Croatia is also facing a radical reform of the pension system, which is in a state of near collapse.

Penic said some of the companies must be restructured, such as loss-making INA (Industrija Nafte) oil company, while others like the state telecoms monopolist HPT were very profitable and attractive to foreign investors. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
